newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish advertising spending set for fast growth.
newsitem.headline: Polish advertising spending set for fast growth.

text.p: Total spending on advertising in Poland grew 40 percent in 1996 to two billion zlotys and the trend is likely to continue for several years, the head of a media house which monitors the Polish market, said on Thursday.
"In 1996 advertisers spent in Poland more than two billion zlotys, against about 1.4 billion zlotys spent in 1995," Jakub Biezynski of Optimus Media said.

Biezynski said that according to Amer Nielsen Research (ANR), which surveys the Polish advertising market, television advertising accounted for the most of expenditures with 1.2 billion zlotys spent in 1996 and 810 million in 1995.
Spending on print media amounted to 640 million zlotys in 1996 and 430 million in 1995.

Biezynski said the Polish advertising market should continue to expand quickly because the current levels of spending on advertising compared with the purchasing power of consumers was among the lowest in Europe.
He said expected growth in the next five to 10 years should allow the Polish market to reach saturation levels similar to other European countries.

Now advertising spending accounts for 0.5 percent of gross domestic product, while in Hungary and the Czech Republic they represent one percent of GDP and in Western Europe account for 0.7-0.8 percent of GDP.

Biezynski said that because Poland's advertising market was developing from a very low starting point, it grew 440 percent in the last three years compared with 60-percent growth rates in the Czech Republic or Slovenia.
